notes.title: 24th of November, 2023 - Patch 1.04

Thanks again for your continued support and patience!

notes.title: 9th of November, 2023 - Patch 1.02
notes.notes:
Hi there everyone, today we're publishing the 2nd patch for Project Regolith, addressing a number of missing colliders, some issues with world-space portals, a missing achievement trigger, and some other things! Check out our full patch notes below:

[u][b]Project Regolith Update, 9th of November, 2023 - Patch 1.02[/b][/u]
- Fixed a massive performance issue being caused by a check that should've only been run once on the Main Menu. Framerates should be a little more stable on all machines now.

- Made some adjustments to the player's cameras to (hopefully) reduce noticeable clipping through world-space portals.

- Fixed an issue that was preventing an achievement related to [spoiler]the Atrium doors opening, revealing Cronus X[/spoiler] from firing.

- Restored a missing label from the players' settings menus for Caption Opacity. This was previously labelled correctly on the main menu but not during gameplay.

- Fixed an issue that was causing some specific Puzzle-related objects, such as the [spoiler]"Unstable" Model Car in the Admin Puzzle[/spoiler] being respawned in the wrong place when using the "Respawn Objects" pause menu button.

- Updated a few interaction prompts that were displaying the default placeholder "Interact With This Thing" text to display the correct prompt instead.

- Updated some of the prompts on the [spoiler]Terraforming Puzzle's interactable terminals[/spoiler] to better reflect some components that can be interacted with.

- Fixed a number of missing collision issues.

- Fixed some world-space portals being culled/not rendering at incorrect times.

- Fixed the Key Rebinding Settings tab in the Main Menu not displaying the unchangeable bindings for "Display Directive", "Open Codex", and "Text Chat".

- Fixed the End Credits UI being displayed smaller than intended.

- Fixed a missing sound cue on the [spoiler]Atrium Viewing Shutter[/spoiler], more door-related missing SFX fixes will be coming with next week's patch!

----------------------------------------------------------------------

That's all for this week - We're aiming to have another patch next week addressing some more noticeable world-space portal culling, as well as some general level culling/pop-in and out issues with the map.

Thanks for your patience,
- Conor and the Regolith Team

notes.title: Project Regolith - Patch 1.01, 3rd of November, 2023
notes.notes:
Hi there folks, we've pushed Project Regolith's first bug-fix patch, aiming at addressing some of the known issues we've spotted since launch a couple of days ago.

3rd of November, 2023 - Patch 1.01:
- Fixed the final puzzle's music cues overlapping the closing music in the game's end sequence.
- Fixed the controls responsible for [spoiler]scuttling the station[/spoiler] not correctly triggering a music cue.
- Moved Crew Log #11 (AKA [spoiler]Nerd Rage[/spoiler]) out of it's confinement near the [spoiler]Terraforming Labs[/spoiler].
- Fixed broken material on the [spoiler]Terraforming Test Tube[/spoiler]'s [spoiler]refined quantum energy[/spoiler] seen during the [spoiler]Terraforming Lab[/spoiler] puzzle.
- Removed an oversized trigger in [spoiler]Terraforming[/spoiler] that was causing LightBot to teleport somewhere he shouldn't, softlocking the game.
- Implemented a fix for rare cases of the [spoiler]Station Control Arming Keys[/spoiler] not spawning correctly during the [spoiler]Admin[/spoiler] puzzle.
- (Hopefully) Fixed an issue with loading the game from some checkpoints immediately crashing the host out of the scene. If you have any issues loading from checkpoints, please submit a bug report either in-game or via our Discord!
- Attempting a fix for some players having their FPS locked to 20 - Not 100% certain that this will work, so if you're feeling like your framerate is locked in-game to a low value, please report it in our Discord or in the Steam Discussions!

notes.title: An Important Update Regarding Launch
notes.notes:
[h3]Hey everyone, we'd like to share an update regarding the planned launch of Project Regolith.[/h3]

These past few weeks we've been promoting that Project Regolith would be launching this Friday, the 27th of October. We've been committed to this date for the past couple of months, but unfortunately, there's been a series of hiccups in Steam's build review process, and it's looking like we're not going to be approved for release by Valve's team in time to hit our deadline.

To be fully transparent about the issue:
Early this morning we were notified that the Steam Review Team has been having connectivity issues that we hadn't yet encountered in our testing and review build of the game that we were planning to set live tomorrow. After a lot of experimentation today we're fairly confident we've ID'd the problem and implemented a fix, BUT this fix still needs to go through Steam's review process again, which can take a few days depending on their queue density.


[h3]So, what does this mean for launch?[/h3]

Unless we get a miraculous reply from the Steam team early tomorrow morning during their office hours declaring that they're no longer having the connection problem, [b]it seems we'll be pushing back launch by a few days at the very least.[/b]

We're fully aware of how frustrating this may be for those of you who've been keen to get your hands on the game, and trust me when I say that nobody's more frustrated at the situation than us.

Admittedly, blame for this issue lies on us as a team for leaving this review process so late, and not accounting for potential tech issues on Steam's end.

I know this sucks to hear, and it definitely sucks to write - So we'd like to apologize to you all for the delay. The moment we have more info we'll be sharing it via our [url=https://discord.gg/EpwKaVbJfk]Discord[/url].

- The Regolith Team

notes.title: Public Devlog #9 - VA Update, The TC Corp, and Outpost Rhea
notes.notes:
[h3]Hey there once again folks, welcome to this fortnight's devlog
[/h3]
If you're up to date with [url=https://steamcommunity.com/games/2220420/announcements/detail/3721705159484642501] our last post[/url], you'd know that we'll have wrapped up our VA Casting process! Today I'd like to give you all a short update on what's next for Casting, and go in-depth on the driving force behind the events of the game - The TerraCaelum Corporation - and their deep space magnum opous, Outpost Rhea, the location you'll find yourselves exploring throughout Project Regolith.


[h2]VA Update[/h2]
Over the past couple of weeks, Conor and I finished listening through, categorizing, and parring down our massive list of over 300 auditions, and subsequent 80-ish callbacks! We've been having preliminary meetings with our choices for main cast members, and we're planning to publish an official cast list once we've finished making sure everyone's on-board! look forward to that during the next devlog!


[h2]The TerraCaelum Corporation[/h2]
The TerraCaelum Corporation (or TCC for short) are at the forefront of Project Regolith's narrative, an Earth-based private company with their reach beginning to extend into the stars - TCC contracts a multitude of Earth's best corporate and scientific minds with the goal of extending Humanity's borders beyond Sol.

As Humans developed spacefaring technology and began to establish larger, more purpose-built space stations throughout our home in the Sol System, the executives at TCC began dreaming up plans for a deep-space research facility where their contractors could perform advanced studies and help further Human understanding of foreign worlds. This station was dubbed "Outpost Rhea", named for the Engineer who headed the planning and blueprinting of the Station's first iteration.


[h2]Outpost Rhea[/h2]
As decades passed, Outpost Rhea's operations have expanded significantly - with a fresh batch of staff arriving every couple of years in "Rotation Vessels", large autopiloted transport ships that make the 5-year-long trip to and from Rhea to deliver personnel in cryo-sleep. These new crew members pursue a multitude of ventures, answering to a select few superiors whom in turn report to the Director of Operations aboard Rhea, Gustavo Dos Reis Castro.

Recent years aboard Rhea have been eventful, following the discovery of a peculiar space-time anomaly that has seen most of the crew's efforts shift in focus on the orders of Director Castro, and Rhea's Chief Science Officer, Gary Langden, who see an opportunity to develop a new cutting-edge piece of technology.

Feeling a major breakthrough coming, Castro and Langden authorize a new experiment, one that is sure to cement their legacies and validate their time aboard Outpost Rhea. An experiment that would be dubbed [b]"Project Regolith"[/b]...


... Buuuuut that's all we're telling you guys for now! We'll see you all in a couple of weeks for our exciting cast reveal!

As always, don't forget to hit up our socials!
[url=https://twitter.com/Regolith_Int]Twitter[/url] - [url=https://www.instagram.com/regolith_interactive/]Instagram[/url] - [url=https://www.tiktok.com/@regolith_interactive]TikTok[/url] (Content Soon!) - [url=https://www.linkedin.com/company/89682847/]LinkedIn[/url] - [url=https://www.youtube.com/@Regolith_Interactive]YouTube[/url]

'Till next time,

- Ryan

notes.title: Public Devlog #8 - The Bots, VA Casting Progress Update
notes.notes:
[h2]Hello once again, and welcome to this week's community update!
[/h2]

The past couple weeks have been eventful for us here in the office - We've been hard at work categorizing, reviewing, and sending out callbacks for our VA Casting process as outlined in our post from [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/2220420/view/7073508075346322566] a few weeks ago.[/url]

We've got an update on the VA process for you all, as well as a look at the two stars of Project Regolith, the player characters themselves - The Hermes-class LPM (Lightweight Planetary Mapper), and the Hephaestus-class HIL (Heavyweight Industrial Loader), although members of our[url=https://discord.gg/KkNxqHduxJ] Discord [/url] may know them better by their dev nicknames, LightBot and HeavyBot!


[h2]VA Casting Progress Update[/h2]
Initially when we outlined our goals for VA Casting, we had set a casting deadline for the 1st of May, what we hadn't accounted for was the sheer number of people we'd end up receiving interest from. Sitting at just over 300 audition reels, myself and Conor have been listening to, reviewing, and categorizing dozens upon dozens of actors each day - And while we've completed the Callback phase for the game's cast, we were a couple of days behind schedule for two of the roles that had the most auditions sent in.

In the long run, this shouldn't cause any major issues. Casting for a majority of roles will be done on-schedule, and the remainder will be done less than a week following that.

We've been incredibly impressed by a lot of the auditions we've heard so far, and we can't wait to share the names and work of our final cast in a few weeks time!


[h2]The Robots from Rhea[/h2]

[h3]The LightBot - Hermes-Class Lightweight Planetary Mapper[/h3]

[code][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43307026/553bf8276dab4733856b2e8c22fa336add15394b.png[/img]
                                           [i]The Hermes-Class LPM[/i][/code]
Originally designed for remote planetary exploration, the LPM, or "LightBot" as it's become known to the crew of Outpost Rhea is a small, highly maneuverable robot that makes use of several small hydrogen-based thrusters to remain airborne.

The Terra-Caelum Corporation had initially commissioned dozens of these bots for use in Outpost Rhea's experiments, although as the Station's focus shifted away from interplanetary exploration and more towards deep-space research, many of the units were shipped back Earthside and the few that remained were retrofitted to assist with menial labor and tight-space maintenance aboard the station.

The LPM's smaller frame and maneuverability allow it to traverse areas that the Human crew have difficulty reaching, such as crawlspaces, vents, and maintenance shafts.


[h3]The HeavyBot - Hephaestus-Class Heavyweight Industrial Loader[/h3]

[code][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43307026/e7abc8e76161fe0ddff089ec217dcb324dcb2672.png[/img]
                                           [i]The Hephaestus-Class HIL[/i][/code]
Built for use on heavy-duty construction sites, the Hephaestus HIL had assisted Terra-Caelum's many construction efforts in the Sol system, and when it came time for Outpost Rhea's construction, it just made sense to bring a handful out into deep-space with them.

Primarily tasked with hauling or towing overweight materials and machinery throughout the station, the HIL Units were also retrofitted to operate much of the station's infrastructure and technology to help make expansion of Rhea's frame more autonomous and less risky for their fleshy Human counterparts in the Engineering department. As the crew began to rely on the Hephaestus-class more and more, they earned the affectionate nickname "Hephty", or in some other cases, just "HeavyBot".

As part of this autonomy, and since the HIL Units were intended for use in hazardous environments, they are able to bypass many of the Station's quarantine shields, as well as access areas of the station where only high-level executives of TC Corp. are allowed.


Together, Players will take on the role of one of these bots and explore the calamity that left Outpost Rhea abandoned...


[h2]That's all for this week! [/h2]
I'll be back in another two weeks to cover what's next for our VA Cast, and hopefully give you all some names! But 'till then, take care of yourselves!

[url=https://discord.gg/KkNxqHduxJ] Did you know we have a Discord where you can chat with us and members of the community?[/url] 
It'd mean a lot of us if you joined!

notes.title: Public Devlog #04 - Delay News and a Short Update
notes.notes:
Hello again everyone!

We were hoping to be able to share some better news at this stage but unfortunately we're still waiting on updates regarding our new office space, as well as on some other fronts that I'll be discussing today.

If you have read our [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/2220420/view/3666529724079722183]last devlog,[/url] you'd know that we have officially made the decision to delay the game a little later into Q3 of this year, aiming ideally for the end of August. A number of factors have contributed to this; The team being forced to work out of home, our applications for further funding from Government Sources here in Australia, and the work that has stemmed from these processes have had an impact on the time we've been able to dedicate to the game, and here's why:

[h2]Working From Home[/h2]
Game development is a very collaborative medium - As such, working remotely impacts efficiency of communications and workflows, as well as leaves us more susceptible to software, hardware, and network issues. We're hoping to get good news soon and finally move into our office space, but until then, we're stuck working in this reduced capacity.

[h2]Funding Applications[/h2]
Since mid-December of 2022, we've been looking into external funding from two Government departments here in Australia, VicScreens (who are in charge of funding on a State level here in Victoria), and ScreenAustralia (the Federal counterpart that operates for Australia at large). These processes have seen us attending meetings, drafting new documentation, and filling in application forms for the better part of the past two months - The endgame for these applications is being able to pay the team a proper salary and allow us to leave our part-time work to focus on Regolith fully.
We've recently completed all our applications and are now just waiting on review processes - hopefully there will be more to share on this front in the coming month.

[h2]To Briefly Summarize[/h2]
Since the beginning of 2023 we've had a lot of extra stuff on our plate to handle outside of the game, and we're working through it as best we can - However, due to the amount of time we've lost as a result, we made the difficult decision to delay.
We hope you all understand, and we'll continue to keep you updated as important changes occur.

[h2]Project Update[/h2]
Setbacks aside, we'd like to take this time to share another couple of WIP screenshots from the game!

[hr][/hr]

That's all for now, see you all in a couple of weeks with some (hopefully) more exciting news! As always, remember to follow our socials if you haven't already!

notes.title: Public Devlog #03 - Progress Update and Planned Launch Window
notes.notes:
Hey everyone! Another couple of weeks has passed, and that means it's time for another update!

If you missed the last post where we went into a little more detail about our background as a team, you can find it [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/2220420/view/3666528457176905090]HERE[/url]. As for this week, I'll be updating you guys on where we're at with moving into our new office space, talking a little about our planned release window for the game, and sharing some progress since our last update!

[h2]Office Update[/h2]
Since the beginning of the year, we've been waiting to move into a new office space in the Melbourne CBD - Unfortunately, there's been a slew of logistics issues that have gotten in the way of us moving in, and that's meant that for the past 6 weeks we've been working out of home. These issues have also taken a bit of a bite out of our time on the project, as well as some other things I'll cover shortly.

Hopefully in the near future we'll be able to share some photos once we're moved into the space, but for now, we'll be continuing to work out of home.

[h2]Release Window[/h2]
Initially when we hosted Project Regolith on Kickstarter, we set out with plans to launch in the third-quarter of 2023. We had hoped to be ready-to-go by the end of July, but it's looking more like end of August for the launch of the game right now. There's a couple of reasons, the primary one being that we're still only able to work part-time on the game, pending outcomes from State and Federal funding authorities here in Australia - So most of the team has to split their time between Regolith, and other part-time work to make ends meet.

But we're still committed to our Q3 2023 deadline, and you can expect the full game no later than then!

[h2]Progress Update[/h2]
Despite the recent setbacks, we've still been plugging away towards our initial Alpha milestone, and the game is looking better than ever!

Brandon's been hard at work on some of our upcoming puzzle areas, and we'd like to share a peek at what's to come!

[hr][/hr]

Exciting stuff! But we don't want to give too much away, so we'll leave it there for now! I'll be back in a couple week's time to share some more!
